title: Does private preschool really give children a head start?
summary: In rural India, children in private preschools learn far more than those in public ones. Unequal access to private preschools explains most of the learning gap between richer and poorer children at school entry.

title: Can a one-hour documentary change long-term economic behaviour?
summary: A randomised trial in rural Ethiopia found that a single one-hour screening of documentaries featuring relatable role models produced lasting increases in farm investment, schooling, and household wealth five years on.

title: Rethinking multiple hypothesis testing: A welfare-based approach

title: How AI can put 20 years of development evidence to work
summary: A new playbook from J-PAL argues that AI's value in development lies not in the technology itself but in how well it is grafted onto decades of existing evidence about what improves lives.

title: Can bank access help farmers weather climate shocks?
summary: India's 1980s rural bank branch expansion only had modest effects on average agricultural output, but it substantially reduced farmers' vulnerability to adverse rainfall shocks, largely by helping them sustain irrigation.

title: The birth of Bangladesh: How the Bhola cyclone fostered revolution
summary: New research using satellite data on the 1970 Bhola cyclone shows that the storm's uneven intensity across East Pakistan increased support for the Awami League and recruitment of freedom fighters, helping tip the balance toward Bangladesh's independence.

title: How financial aid could transform student welfare in sub-Saharan Africa
summary: College students in sub-Saharan Africa can be as food insecure as the ultra-poor, but modest financial support may yield large returns for wellbeing.

title: How an environmental documentary reshaped China’s land markets

summary: When tax enforcement depends on geography, firms may choose to locate where taxes are easier to evade rather than where they are most productive. A Chinese reform that standardised VAT enforcement across rugged and flatter counties reduced this misallocation, raising aggregate p…

title: Does making formality less costly actually pay off?
summary: By making formalisation cheaper and easier, Brazil’s MEI programme helped millions of microentrepreneurs register – but delivered little in higher earnings, functioning instead as a subsidised expansion of social security access at a net fiscal cost.

title: Why businesses stay small in emerging markets
summary: New research explains why businesses in developing economies remain smaller and grow more slowly than their counterparts in advanced economies – pointing to regulatory hurdles, credit constraints, and measurement challenges as key culprits.

title: Do language barriers hold back agricultural development?
summary: In rural India, language barriers restrict farmers' access to digital agricultural advice, hindering technology adoption and reducing crop yields.

title: The informal sector: Why some economies are almost entirely hidden
summary: The informal economy – accounting for 30–90% of the labour force across developing countries – remains largely invisible to governments, undermining tax revenue, productivity, and long-term growth, and requires a combined strategy of easing formalisation costs while raising enfo…

title: Can forecasting social science make experiments better?
summary: Evidence from 100 Social Science Prediction Platform projects shows that research forecasts are too optimistic on average, but still predictive enough to improve study design when they are combined, shrunk, and weighted carefully.

title: How economic ideas shape the way governments deliver policy
summary: New evidence from colonial India shows how economic ideas can influence civil servants and shape policy for decades, determining whether governments respond decisively to crisis or not at all.
